title: Amplification and Pooling
author: Franziska Aron
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.beqkjduw
materials: Amplify in a thermocycler with the following program: Adjust the number of cycles according to the amplification factor as calculated in step 1. During this incubation take MinElute columns out of the fridge so they warm up to room temperature before use in the next step. This is an ideal point to prepare downstream steps, including labelling of final elution tubes, MinElute Columns etc.
Put column into new 1.5 mL LoBind tubes.
Prepare cleaned workspace with all necessary reagents and equipment. Label all 0.2 mL PCR strips for the PCR reactions.

steps.title: Calculate required PCR cycles
steps.instruction: Based on the quantified copies per reaction, compute the number of cycles needed to reach 10^13 copies using the formula LOG((1*10^13 / copies per rxn),2). Do not exceed 1.4 × 10^13 copies to avoid heteroduplexes. If the calculation yields fewer than 3 cycles, you may reduce the input volume to <5 µL. Instead of four 5 µL reactions you may split into eight 2 µL reactions.

steps.title: Set up four 100 µL PCRs
steps.instruction: For each indexed library, prepare four amplification reactions of 100 µL total volume.

steps.title: Prepare master mix
steps.instruction: Vortex the master mix, add the polymerase enzyme, then mix by pipetting or inverting the tube.

steps.title: Add mastermix and library
steps.instruction: Pipette 95 µL of the prepared mastermix and 5 µL of the indexed library into each 0.2 mL PCR strip tube. Keep any remaining library at –20 °C.

steps.title: Purify PCR product with MinElute
steps.instruction: Use one MinElute column for the combined four 100 µL reactions (≈400 µL total).

substeps.instruction: Add 2400 µL PB or PBI buffer to a 5 mL tube (600 µL per reaction), combine the four PCR reactions, vortex briefly. The PBI should remain yellow; purple indicates high pH and compromised column performance.
Add 700 µL PE wash buffer to the column, spin at 15800 × g for 1 min at room temperature, discard flow‑through.
Add 50 µL EBT buffer to the centre of the filter, incubate 2 min, spin at 15800 × g for 1 min, collect eluate. Pipette EBT directly onto the membrane centre without touching the membrane.
If the entire mixture has not yet passed through, repeat the loading steps (add buffer, incubate, spin) until all sample has been processed.
Perform a final dry spin at 15800 × g for 1 min.

During loading, handle waste carefully: discard flow‑through into a waste tube, pat the collection‑tube rim dry on a single spot of paper tissue, avoid touching the rim with the waste container, and clean the work surface after all samples.

steps.title: Dilute 1:10 and assess library
steps.instruction: Dilute the purified indexed library 1:10 with HPLC‑water. Check fragment size, concentration, and heteroduplexes using the D1000 TapeStation kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Reconditioning PCR (if heteroduplexes)
steps.instruction: If heteroduplexes are detected, set up a 100 µL Herculase PCR with 100 ng library template and run a single cycle: 95 °C 2 min, 58 °C 2 min, 72 °C 5 min. Purify the product with the MinElute protocol above, eluting in 20 µL EBT.

steps.title: Dilute to 10 nM and pool libraries
steps.instruction: Dilute each amplified indexed library to 10 nM using EBT buffer or HPLC‑water. Pool the libraries in equal volumes to obtain an equimolar pool; the final pool concentration should be 10 nM.

steps.title: Verify final library concentration
steps.instruction: Check the 10 nM library or pooled library concentration with the High‑Sensitivity D1000 TapeStation kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
